name: Engineering
dimension: the physical balance that closes an artefact model

objects.label: Force and deformation
objects.text: EN.O.A1 Force and deformation

objects.label: Rigid bodies
objects.text: EN.O.A1.1 Rigid bodies. Statics: ΣF = 0 and ΣM = 0 when inertia is negligible. Dynamics: ΣF = m a and ΣM = dH/dt about the centre of mass or a fixed point. These laws are Newtonian mechanics (uses PH.O.A1.1). EN owns the free-body reduction and determinacy check.

objects.label: Free-body diagram, determinacy
objects.text: EN.O.A1.1.1 Free-body diagram and static determinacy.

objects.label: Mechanism dynamics
objects.text: EN.O.A1.1.2 Rigid-body dynamics of mechanisms (linkages, gears, cams).

objects.label: Lumped vibration models
objects.text: EN.O.A1.1.3 Lumped vibration models: single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems with linear springs and viscous damping. Natural frequency ωn = √(k/m) for an undamped linear oscillator.

objects.label: Slender members
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2 Slender members. A member whose length greatly exceeds its section is reduced to section resultants plus a kinematic assumption.

objects.label: Euler–Bernoulli beam
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.1 Euler–Bernoulli beam. For a prismatic, linear-elastic member with small slopes and plane sections remaining plane and normal: EI d²v/dx² = M(x). With load q positive downward, dM/dx = V and dV/dx = −q (Gere and Goodno, §4.5; sign convention stated, audit fact check).

objects.label: Timoshenko beam
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.2 Timoshenko beam: adds shear deformation and rotary inertia for deep or short beams.

objects.label: Torsion of circular shaft
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.3 Torsion of a circular shaft. For a linear-elastic, circular or annular, prismatic bar under small twist: T = G J θ / L and τ = T r / J.

objects.label: Euler column buckling
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.4 Euler column buckling. For an initially straight, slender, linear-elastic, centrally loaded column: Pcr = π² E I / (K L)². Stocky columns leave this formula for a tangent-modulus or code curve.

objects.label: Kirchhoff–Love and Mindlin–Reissner plates
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.5 Kirchhoff–Love plate and Mindlin–Reissner plate. Kirchhoff–Love applies to thin plates with normals staying normal; Mindlin–Reissner admits transverse shear for moderately thick plates.

objects.label: Thin-walled pressure vessel
objects.text: EN.O.A1.2.6 Thin-walled pressure vessel. For wall thickness much less than radius, under internal pressure p: hoop stress pr/t and longitudinal stress pr/2t.

objects.label: Deformable continua
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3 Deformable continua. The parent theory when section assumptions fail.

objects.label: Cauchy stress and traction
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.1 Cauchy stress and traction t = σᵀn (uses PH.O.A1.5 for the continuum balance laws).

objects.label: Isotropic linear elasticity (Hooke)
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.2 Isotropic linear elasticity (Hooke). For small strain, a linear, isotropic material: σ = λ tr(ε) I + 2μ ε, with G = E / 2(1+ν). Uses PH.O.A1.5.

objects.label: Tresca and von Mises yield
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.3 Yield criteria: Tresca (maximum shear) and von Mises (distortion energy), for isotropic ductile metals under quasi-static load.

objects.label: Mohr's circle
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.4 Mohr's circle: principal stresses and maximum shear from the plane-stress transformation.

objects.label: LEFM, KIc
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.5 Linear-elastic fracture mechanics. Under small-scale yielding, K = Y σ √(π a). Mode I, plane-strain failure occurs when K reaches KIc (ASTM E399).

objects.label: Fatigue life, Paris law
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.6 Fatigue life. Basquin (stress-life) and Coffin–Manson (strain-life) relations, fitted per material. Paris law da/dN = C (ΔK)^m holds in region II only; C and m depend on material and R-ratio (Paris and Erdogan 1963).

objects.label: Effective stress, Mohr–Coulomb (CONTESTED)
objects.text: EN.O.A1.3.7 Geomechanics. Terzaghi effective stress σ′ = σ − u for saturated soil. Mohr–Coulomb strength τ = c′ + σ′ tan φ′ for drained soil and rock joints. CONTESTED: EA.O.A1 (rock and soil as earth materials) is the alternative owner; EN keeps the strength closure, EA owns genesis.

objects.label: Contact interfaces
objects.text: EN.O.A1.4 Contact interfaces.

objects.label: Hertz contact (CONTESTED)
objects.text: EN.O.A1.4.1 Hertz contact. For two smooth, elastic, non-conforming bodies with frictionless contact and small contact area: contact radius and peak pressure follow from load, curvatures and moduli. CONTESTED: PH.O.A1.5 is the alternative owner.

objects.label: Coulomb friction
objects.text: EN.O.A1.4.2 Coulomb friction: tangential force bounded by μ times normal force, an empirical closure.

objects.label: Archard wear
objects.text: EN.O.A1.4.3 Archard wear law: worn volume proportional to load times sliding distance over hardness, with a fitted wear coefficient (UNVERIFIED as to standard notation).

objects.label: Contact and member concepts
objects.text: EN.O.A1.4.4 Concepts: stress concentration, Saint-Venant decay, shear centre, slenderness, ductility, redundancy, mechanism.

objects.label: Mass and momentum
objects.text: EN.O.A2 Mass and momentum

objects.label: Internal flows
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1 Internal flows.

objects.label: Bernoulli (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.1 Bernoulli equation along a streamline, for steady, inviscid, incompressible flow: p/ρ + V²/2 + g z = constant. Uses PH.O.A1.5. A loss term is added, not derived, when the hypotheses fail.

objects.label: Darcy–Weisbach
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.2 Darcy–Weisbach head loss h_f = f (L/D) V²/2g, where f is the Darcy (Moody) friction factor, four times the Fanning factor.

objects.label: Colebrook, Moody, minor losses
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.3 Colebrook equation and Moody chart for f in fully developed turbulent pipe flow (empirical closure). Minor losses K V²/2g.

objects.label: Pump–system matching, affinity laws
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.4 Pump and fan matching: head-capacity curve against system curve. Affinity laws hold only between dynamically similar operating points.

objects.label: Reynolds lubrication equation
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.5 Reynolds lubrication equation, for thin, viscous, laminar films with negligible inertia (tribology).

objects.label: Euler turbomachine equation
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.6 Euler turbomachine equation. For steady flow through a rotor, specific work done on the fluid is w = u₂c_θ2 − u₁c_θ1 (pump or compressor); for a turbine the extracted work is its negative.

objects.label: Joukowsky surge
objects.text: EN.O.A2.1.7 Water hammer (Joukowsky surge Δp = ρ a ΔV for instantaneous valve closure in an elastic pipe).

objects.label: External flows
objects.text: EN.O.A2.2 External flows. Drag and lift coefficients; boundary layer; separation as the stall and form-drag mechanism. Reynolds number Re = ρVL/μ = UL/ν (the two forms are equivalent, uses PH.O.A1.5). Flight mechanics and aeroelasticity draw on this cell plus EN.O.A1.

objects.label: Free-surface flows
objects.text: EN.O.A2.3 Free-surface flows.

objects.label: Specific energy, Froude number
objects.text: EN.O.A2.3.1 Open-channel specific energy and Froude number Fr = V/√(g h) for a rectangular channel.

objects.label: Manning equation
objects.text: EN.O.A2.3.2 Manning equation, an empirical resistance closure for steady, uniform, fully rough open-channel flow.

objects.label: Ship hydrostatics and stability
objects.text: EN.O.A2.3.3 Ship hydrostatics and stability: buoyancy, metacentric height GM, righting arm, for small heel angles (initial stability).

objects.label: Hull resistance, seakeeping
objects.text: EN.O.A2.3.4 Hull resistance and seakeeping, with Froude scaling of wave resistance.

objects.label: Compressible and acoustic flows
objects.text: EN.O.A2.4 Compressible and acoustic flows.

objects.label: Isentropic nozzle, choking
objects.text: EN.O.A2.4.1 Isentropic nozzle relations for a calorically perfect gas in adiabatic, reversible, quasi-one-dimensional flow. Choked flow when the throat is sonic (M = 1).

objects.label: Normal-shock relations
objects.text: EN.O.A2.4.2 Normal-shock relations (Rankine–Hugoniot) for a perfect gas.

objects.label: Linear acoustics
objects.text: EN.O.A2.4.3 Linear acoustics: small-amplitude pressure waves in a quiescent fluid; sound pressure level and transmission loss (noise control).

objects.label: Porous-medium flows
objects.text: EN.O.A2.5 Porous-medium flows.

objects.label: Darcy's law (CONTESTED)
objects.text: EN.O.A2.5.1 Darcy's law q = −(k/μ)∇p for slow, laminar flow through a rigid, saturated porous medium. CONTESTED: EA.O.A4 (groundwater) is the alternative owner.

objects.label: Ergun equation
objects.text: EN.O.A2.5.2 Ergun equation for pressure drop through a packed bed of particles.

objects.label: Terzaghi consolidation
objects.text: EN.O.A2.5.3 Consolidation (Terzaghi one-dimensional consolidation) for saturated, linear, laterally confined soil.

objects.label: Energy and entropy
objects.text: EN.O.A3 Energy and entropy

objects.label: First-law balances
objects.text: EN.O.A3.1 First-law balances.

objects.label: Steady open first law
objects.text: EN.O.A3.1.1 Steady open-system first law: Q̇ − Ẇ = Σṁ(h + V²/2 + g z)out − Σṁ(h + V²/2 + g z)in, with heat in and work out positive. The law is owned by physics (uses PH.O.A4.1).

objects.label: Property closures
objects.text: EN.O.A3.1.2 Property closures: ideal-gas model, steam and refrigerant tables (data, W12 and W4).

objects.label: Power and refrigeration cycles
objects.text: EN.O.A3.1.3 Cycles as applications: Rankine, Brayton, Otto, Diesel (air-standard idealisations), vapour-compression refrigeration with COP = Q_cold / W.

objects.label: Second-law limits
objects.text: EN.O.A3.2 Second-law limits.

objects.label: Carnot efficiency (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A3.2.1 Carnot efficiency 1 − T_c/T_h, the ceiling for a heat engine between two reservoirs at absolute temperatures. Uses PH.O.A4.1.

objects.label: Exergy
objects.text: EN.O.A3.2.2 Exergy: work potential relative to a stated dead state. Irreversibility located per component, not only totalled.

objects.label: Pinch analysis
objects.text: EN.O.A3.2.3 Pinch analysis: minimum approach temperature in a heat-exchanger network.

objects.label: Heat-transfer rates
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3 Heat-transfer rates.

objects.label: Fourier conduction (CONTESTED)
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3.1 Fourier's law q = −k∇T for an isotropic conductor; plane wall Q = k A ΔT / L at steady state. CONTESTED: PH.O.A4.1 (transport) is the alternative owner.

objects.label: Newton cooling, Nusselt correlations
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3.2 Newton's law of cooling q = h A (T_s − T_∞), with h from a Nusselt correlation used inside its stated Re and Pr range.

objects.label: Radiation exchange
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3.3 Radiation exchange. Emissive power of a grey surface is ε σ T⁴. Net exchange of a small grey surface with large surroundings is q = ε σ A (T_s⁴ − T_sur⁴), absolute temperatures (Incropera and DeWitt, ch. 1). Enclosures use view factors.

objects.label: LMTD, effectiveness–NTU
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3.4 Heat exchangers: LMTD method, or effectiveness–NTU with NTU = U A / C_min.

objects.label: Fins
objects.text: EN.O.A3.3.5 Fins: added area against a convection boundary, with fin efficiency.

objects.label: Reacting energy
objects.text: EN.O.A3.4 Reacting energy. Heating value and stoichiometry enter the first law as an enthalpy of reaction (uses CH.O.A3.1). Adiabatic flame temperature is the no-heat-loss limit. Fire growth and smoke models for compartments draw on this cell (fire protection).

objects.label: Electromagnetic state
objects.text: EN.O.A4 Electromagnetic state

objects.label: Lumped circuits
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1 Lumped circuits. Valid when the circuit is small compared with the shortest relevant wavelength.

objects.label: Ohm, Kirchhoff (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.1 Ohm's law V = I R for a linear resistor; Kirchhoff circuit laws (uses PH.O.A1.2b).

objects.label: Impedance and phasors
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.2 Impedance R, jωL and 1/(jωC), with phasors, for linear circuits in sinusoidal steady state.

objects.label: Thévenin and Norton
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.3 Thévenin and Norton equivalents, for linear networks seen from two terminals.

objects.label: Maximum power transfer (conjugate)
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.4 Maximum power transfer. For a linear source with impedance Z_s, load power is maximised when Z_L = Z_s* (complex conjugate). A resistive match applies only to DC or purely resistive sources. A theorem, not a universal design rule.

objects.label: LTI response, state space
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.5 Linear time-invariant system response: impulse response, transfer function, frequency response. Fourier and Laplace transforms are MA (uses MA.O.A4). State space ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du and G(s) = C(sI − A)⁻¹B + D, for LTI plants.

objects.label: Sampling theorem (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.6 Sampling theorem. A band-limited signal with no content at or above B is recovered from samples taken faster than 2B per second. Uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 94A).

objects.label: Circuit concepts
objects.text: EN.O.A4.1.7 Concepts: ground and reference, power factor, harmonics, noise figure.

objects.label: Electromechanical conversion
objects.text: EN.O.A4.2 Electromechanical conversion.

objects.label: Magnetic circuit
objects.text: EN.O.A4.2.1 Magnetic circuit: Ampère's law with reluctance, for linear core material without saturation.

objects.label: Ideal transformer
objects.text: EN.O.A4.2.2 Ideal transformer V₁/V₂ = N₁/N₂, for zero leakage, zero winding resistance and infinite core permeability.

objects.label: Machines, synchronous speed, slip
objects.text: EN.O.A4.2.3 Machines: torque from current and flux. Synchronous speed n_s = 120 f / p (rpm, p poles). Induction-motor slip.

objects.label: AC power-flow equations
objects.text: EN.O.A4.2.4 Power-flow equations for an AC network in balanced steady state (load flow).

objects.label: Distributed fields
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3 Distributed fields.

objects.label: Transmission line
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3.1 Transmission line: telegrapher's equations; characteristic impedance; reflection coefficient.

objects.label: Waveguides and antennas
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3.2 Waveguides and antennas: modes, gain, radiation pattern.

objects.label: Friis transmission
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3.3 Friis transmission equation for far-field free-space links between matched, polarisation-aligned antennas.

objects.label: Optical and photonic devices
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3.4 Optical and photonic devices: fibre modes, attenuation, dispersion. Optics as physics (uses PH.O.A1.2c).

objects.label: EMC, skin effect
objects.text: EN.O.A4.3.5 Electromagnetic compatibility: coupling paths and shielding; skin effect.

objects.label: Semiconductor devices
objects.text: EN.O.A4.4 Semiconductor devices.

objects.label: Diode and MOSFET curves
objects.text: EN.O.A4.4.1 Diode and MOSFET constitutive curves (e.g., Shockley diode equation for an ideal p–n junction with low injection).

objects.label: Drift–diffusion device model
objects.text: EN.O.A4.4.2 Drift–diffusion device model (uses PH.O.A4.4a for band theory).

objects.label: Digital abstraction
objects.text: EN.O.A4.4.3 Digital abstraction: voltage bands treated as logic levels, with noise margins. Above this abstraction the claim is CS (uses CS.O.A2.4 for the Boolean function).

objects.label: Switching converters
objects.text: EN.O.A4.4.4 Power-electronic switching converters: averaged models of buck and boost stages in continuous conduction.

objects.label: Composition and microstructure
objects.text: EN.O.A5 Composition and microstructure

objects.label: Reaction rates
objects.text: EN.O.A5.1 Reaction rates.

objects.label: Species balance
objects.text: EN.O.A5.1.1 Species balance: accumulation = in − out + generation.

objects.label: Ideal reactors, RTD
objects.text: EN.O.A5.1.2 Ideal reactors: batch, continuous stirred tank (perfect mixing), plug flow (no axial mixing). Conversion against residence time; residence-time distribution diagnoses real reactors.

objects.label: Arrhenius (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A5.1.3 Arrhenius rate constant k = A exp(−E_a/RT), for an elementary or effective rate over a stated temperature range. Uses CH.O.A4.2.

objects.label: Scale-up limits
objects.text: EN.O.A5.1.4 Scale-up limits: mixing and heat removal.

objects.label: Equilibrium stages
objects.text: EN.O.A5.2 Equilibrium stages.

objects.label: Raoult, fugacity (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A5.2.1 Raoult's law for ideal liquid mixtures, or a fugacity model when non-ideal (uses CH.O.A3.1).

objects.label: McCabe–Thiele
objects.text: EN.O.A5.2.2 McCabe–Thiele construction for binary distillation, assuming constant molar overflow.

objects.label: Two-film theory
objects.text: EN.O.A5.2.3 Two-film theory: interphase flux = K Δc, with an overall coefficient. Rate-based models apply when stage equilibrium fails.

objects.label: Flowsheet degrees of freedom
objects.text: EN.O.A5.2.4 Flowsheet degrees of freedom, recycle and purge.

objects.label: Microstructure–property relations
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3 Microstructure–property relations.

objects.label: Phase diagram (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3.1 Phase diagram as the equilibrium map (uses CH.O.A3.1 for phase equilibrium).

objects.label: TTT and CCT diagrams
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3.2 TTT and CCT diagrams as kinetic maps for steels.

objects.label: Hall–Petch
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3.3 Hall–Petch relation σ_y = σ₀ + k d^(−1/2), for polycrystals over a stated grain-size range (fails at the nanoscale).

objects.label: Rule of mixtures bounds
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3.4 Rule of mixtures for composites, as upper (Voigt) and lower (Reuss) bounds, not a point prediction.

objects.label: Dislocation slip
objects.text: EN.O.A5.3.5 Dislocation slip as the mechanism of plastic flow (uses PH.O.A4.4 condensed matter).

objects.label: Electrochemical cells
objects.text: EN.O.A5.4 Electrochemical cells.

objects.label: Faraday's laws of electrolysis (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A5.4.1 Faraday's laws of electrolysis: mass reacted proportional to charge passed (uses CH.O.A3.1). Applied to corrosion rate and plating.

objects.label: Nernst equation (applied)
objects.text: EN.O.A5.4.2 Nernst equation for the reversible cell potential at stated activities (uses CH.O.A3.1).

objects.label: Battery and fuel-cell models
objects.text: EN.O.A5.4.3 Battery and fuel-cell device models: capacity, polarisation curves, state of charge.

objects.label: Passivation
objects.text: EN.O.A5.4.4 Passivation as a kinetic state, not a permanent property.

objects.label: Neutron balances
objects.text: EN.O.A5.5 Neutron balances.

objects.label: k_eff, criticality
objects.text: EN.O.A5.5.1 Effective multiplication factor k_eff; criticality at k_eff = 1.

objects.label: Neutron diffusion equation
objects.text: EN.O.A5.5.2 One-group neutron diffusion equation, valid away from boundaries and strong absorbers; transport theory otherwise. Cross-section data uses PH.

objects.label: Decay heat
objects.text: EN.O.A5.5.3 Decay heat after shutdown, carried as a source by the energy balance EN.O.A3.1.

objects.label: Shielding attenuation
objects.text: EN.O.A5.5.4 Shielding attenuation for a stated source and geometry.

warrants.standard: Prediction matches test within stated uncertainty; code calibration meets the target reliability index
warrants.defeaters: Hypothesis outside range (slenderness, small strain, linearity); imperfection sensitivity; residual stress; unmodelled failure mode

warrants.standard: Equilibrium closes; determinacy checked
warrants.defeaters: Neglected inertia or flexibility; wrong support idealisation

warrants.standard: Section assumption holds beyond Saint-Venant distance; test agrees
warrants.defeaters: Stocky or short member; local buckling; stress concentration; large slope

warrants.standard: Mesh convergence plus validation test (ASME V&V 10); fracture and fatigue data to ASTM methods
warrants.defeaters: Constitutive law out of range; singularities; LEFM used beyond small-scale yielding; Paris law outside region II

warrants.standard: Measured contact stiffness, friction or wear within scatter band
warrants.defeaters: Conforming geometry; lubrication regime change; surface roughness; fitted coefficient used off-population

warrants.standard: Validation against experiment with stated uncertainty (ASME V&V 20)
warrants.defeaters: Turbulence closure outside calibration; transition; multiphase; non-Newtonian fluid

warrants.standard: Head-loss prediction within correlation scatter; pump test to standard
warrants.defeaters: Developing flow; roughness change; cavitation; Fanning–Darcy confusion

warrants.standard: Wind-tunnel or flight data at matched Re and Mach
warrants.defeaters: Scale effect; transition location; separation not captured

warrants.standard: Model basin or field gauging agreement; Froude similarity respected
warrants.defeaters: Large heel angles; non-uniform flow; scale effect on viscous resistance

warrants.standard: Nozzle and shock data agree; acoustic measurement to standard
warrants.defeaters: Real-gas effects; viscous losses; nonlinear acoustics

warrants.standard: Permeability from test; pressure drop within scatter
warrants.defeaters: Non-Darcy (inertial) regime; heterogeneity; unsaturated medium

warrants.standard: Energy balance closes within measurement uncertainty
warrants.defeaters: Extrapolated correlation; non-equilibrium; wrong dead state

warrants.standard: Balance closes; sign convention stated
warrants.defeaters: Missing stream; stale property data

warrants.standard: Entropy generation non-negative in every component
warrants.defeaters: Wrong reservoir temperatures; dead state undefined

warrants.standard: Correlation used inside its Re/Pr range; test agrees
warrants.defeaters: Fouling; radiation neglected; emissive power used as net exchange

warrants.standard: Calorimetry and flame data agree
warrants.defeaters: Incomplete combustion; dissociation; heat loss

warrants.standard: Prediction matches measurement; compliance test passes
warrants.defeaters: Lumped assumption fails; parasitics; thermal drift

warrants.standard: Measured response within component tolerance
warrants.defeaters: Frequency too high; nonlinearity; resistive match used for complex source

warrants.standard: Machine and transformer tests to IEC/IEEE standard
warrants.defeaters: Saturation; leakage; unbalanced operation

warrants.standard: Field-solver convergence plus range or chamber test
warrants.defeaters: Material dispersion; boundary model; near-field use of Friis

warrants.standard: Device curves within datasheet limits; TCAD calibrated
warrants.defeaters: Temperature drift; high injection; process variation; metastability

warrants.standard: Mass balance closure; pilot-scale agreement; property certificates
warrants.defeaters: Scale-up; impurities; kinetics confused with equilibrium

warrants.standard: Rate data fitted over the operating range; RTD measured
warrants.defeaters: Catalyst deactivation; mixing limits; extrapolated temperature

warrants.standard: Stage efficiency and VLE data agree
warrants.defeaters: Non-ideal mixture treated as ideal; constant molar overflow fails

warrants.standard: Property test certificates; metallography
warrants.defeaters: Microstructure variability; grain size outside Hall–Petch range

warrants.standard: Polarisation and capacity tests
warrants.defeaters: Side reactions; ageing; temperature

warrants.standard: Code validated against critical experiments; benchmark agreement
warrants.defeaters: Cross-section uncertainty; diffusion used near boundaries

bridges_table: EN.B.C1

Civil and environmental engineering: shelter, passage, water and waste on the ground. Sub-bridges: structural, geotechnical, hydraulic, transport, construction, environmental, fire protection, geomatics/surveying, built environment
M.B1, B2, B4 (construction), B5 (partial-factor codes)
ground, buildings, catchments, cities; site claims use EA; aesthetic verdict uses AR; price uses EC
EN.B.C2

Mechanical, aerospace and marine engineering: controlled motion and work. Sub-bridges: machine design, thermal-fluid systems, automotive, aerospace (flight mechanics, aeroelasticity, propulsion, airworthiness), naval architecture and ocean, mechatronics and robotics, acoustics and tribology
O.A1, O.A2, O.A3
M.B2, B3 (control), B4 (manufacture), B5 (type test, certification)
machines, vehicles, aircraft, vessels; orbital mechanics uses PH
EN.B.C3

Electrical and electronic engineering: power and signal transfer. Sub-bridges: power systems, electronics, communications, signal processing, photonics, control implementation, computer engineering (hardware below the ISA), cybersecurity engineering of devices
O.A4
M.B2 (circuit and load-flow), B3, B5 (EMC, IEC/IEEE type test)
grids, devices, links; above the ISA uses CS.O.A2.4; compilers use CS.M.3; protocols use CS.O.A3.4
EN.B.C4

Chemical, materials and resources engineering: change of composition or a specified microstructure, with containment. Sub-bridges: process, separations, reaction, materials and metallurgy, nuclear, petroleum, mining and extractive metallurgy, energy storage
O.A5, with O.A1 (vessel, rock mechanics), O.A3 (heat)
M.B2, B4 (plant), B5 (HAZOP, relief sizing, criticality)
plants, reactors, mines, wells; ore genesis uses EA
EN.B.C5

Industrial and systems engineering: coordinated operation of a human–technical system. Sub-bridges: systems engineering (life-cycle processes, MBSE, interface management, V-model), operations research applied, reliability and safety engineering, human factors, engineering management, manufacturing systems
any O cell as a constraint
M.B1, B3 (optimisation), B5
enterprises, supply chains, fleets; queueing uses MA.O.A5; optimisation uses MA.B.C4; human performance uses MS; cost uses EC/BU

sections.governing_thought: Engineering is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its object claims divide into five balances: force and deformation, mass and momentum, energy and entropy, electromagnetic state, and composition and microstructure.
sections.key_line:
This is the key line of Face O, the claim partition of the pyramid.

- Logic: inductive.
- Plural noun: balances.
- Dimension: the quantity whose balance or constitutive closure finishes the predictive model of an artefact.
- Order: structural, from load path to material.
- Members (5):
  1. force and deformation
  2. mass and momentum
  3. energy and entropy
  4. electromagnetic state
  5. composition and microstructure

Test for a new member (repairs audit EN #18). A sixth balance is warranted only if an artefact model needs a closing quantity none of the five carries. Information state passes that test and is therefore not an EN balance: it is owned by CS (uses CS.O.A2.4). Failure probability also passes it, and is owned by MA (uses MA.O.A5). Neither is held in EN by fiat.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. A formula that predicts behaviour lives on Face O. A discretisation, optimiser or test protocol for it lives on Face M.
2. A law owned by another pyramid is cited, not re-filed: "uses PH.O.A1.5" for Navier–Stokes, Bernoulli, Reynolds number and Hooke.
3. Maxwell's equations, Faraday's law of induction and the Kirchhoff circuit laws: uses PH.O.A1.2b.
4. Second law and Carnot limit: uses PH.O.A4.1. First law in engineering form is cited from the same owner.
5. Arrhenius: uses CH.O.A4.2. Raoult, Nernst and Faraday's laws of electrolysis: uses CH.O.A3.1.
6. Semiconductor band theory: uses PH.O.A4.4a. EN owns the device curve and drift–diffusion device model.
7. Shannon–Hartley capacity and the sampling theorem: uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 94A).
8. Little's law, utilisation ρ = λ/(cμ), Weibull and system reliability: uses MA.O.A5.
9. LP duality, nonlinear optimisation theory and stability criteria: uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 90, 93).
10. Error and convergence of FE, FV and Monte Carlo: uses MA.B.C3. Running them is EN.M.B2.
11. Control theory is a synthesis method (EN.M.B3) on a plant model. It does not add a balance.
12. A code is a calibrated verification shortcut (EN.M.B5, W12). Using a code outside its scope fails verification.
13. Commissioning goes in EN.M.B5; startup goes in EN.M.B4. Prototype test for a closure goes in EN.M.B2; type test against a requirement goes in EN.M.B5.
14. Design choices (endianness, state encoding, degree of reaction) are EN.M.B3 acts, not Face O facts.
15. Software, compilers, protocols and algorithms are CS: EN.B.C3 lists them only as "uses CS.…".
16. Device below the ISA is EN.O.A4.4; the Boolean function is CS.O.A2.4.
17. Biomedical and agricultural engineering are substrate rules on C1–C4, not bridges.
18. Built environment: the artefact meeting its use specification is EN.B.C1; the aesthetic verdict is AR; the site is EA; the price is EC.
19. Contract, liability, product regulation and licensure duty are LA. The engineer's sign-off as a procedure is EN.M.B5.
20. Name collisions are resolved by full names: Euler–Bernoulli beam vs Euler column buckling; Kirchhoff–Love plate vs Kirchhoff circuit laws; Faraday's law of induction vs Faraday's laws of electrolysis.

Coverage: 18 of 19 named groups land fully; 1 partial (4018). 0 refused. 4099 is residual and excluded.

ABET program criteria (31). After the re-cut, the seven "missing" criteria in the audit now land: cybersecurity engineering (C3, uses CS), engineering physics (curriculum; its claims land on Face O cells; no bridge), fire protection (C1, EN.O.A3.4), geological (C4 with rock mechanics; genesis uses EA), naval architecture/marine/ocean (C2, EN.O.A2.3), optical/photonic (C3, EN.O.A4.3.4), surveying (C1). Mining now has rock mechanics (EN.O.A1.3.7). Coverage: 30 of 31 land on a cell, bridge or substrate rule; engineering physics is accounted for as a curriculum, not a bridge. Partial placements remaining: architectural (building services only via C1/A3), engineering management (C5; finance uses BU). These counts are from the audit list and are not re-checked against abet.org here.
sections.validation:
Sizes:
- Key line (Face O): 5.
- Face O cells: 5 A-level + 22 sub-cells = 27 (A1: 4, A2: 5, A3: 4, A4: 4, A5: 5). Named objects (EN.O.Ax.y.z) are leaves, not counted as cells.
- M roles: 5. Sub-groups: B1 3, B2 4, B3 4, B4 4, B5 3.
- Heuristics: 10 (outside count).
- W rows: 27.
- B bridges: 5.

All groups lie within 2–5.

Key-line members, word for word: force and deformation; mass and momentum; energy and entropy; electromagnetic state; composition and microstructure.

Open problems (OPEN):
- OPEN: turbulence closure — no general predictive model of turbulent stress for engineering flows; RANS closures are calibrated models (EN.O.A2).
- OPEN: fatigue under variable-amplitude loading — sequence effects lack a general predictive law (EN.O.A1.3.6).
- OPEN: human reliability quantification — current numbers are heuristic (EN.B.C5; uses MS).

Contested placements (CONTESTED, with alternative):
- CONTESTED: Fourier conduction EN.O.A3.3.1; alternative PH.O.A4.1.
- CONTESTED: Darcy's law EN.O.A2.5.1; alternative EA.O.A4.
- CONTESTED: Hertz contact EN.O.A1.4.1; alternative PH.O.A1.5.
- CONTESTED: Mohr–Coulomb and effective stress EN.O.A1.3.7; alternative EA.O.A1.
- CONTESTED: information state refused to CS; alternative is a sixth EN balance (v1). Rejected because CS owns the state models and a sixth member is not needed.
- CONTESTED: operation folded into EN.M.B4 (actions) and EN.M.B5 (in-service integrity); alternative is a separate "operate and sustain" role, which would give six roles and need regrouping.
- CONTESTED: biomedical and agricultural as substrate rules; alternative is separate bridges (ABET and ANZSRC list biomedical separately).
